key_insight: UniAIR is a unified multimodal AI framework that accurately predicts how mutations alter immune recognition across antibodies, antigens and T cell receptors, enabling cross-context generalization from a single model.
problem_solved: Current mutation-effect predictors are often modality-specific (antibody, antigen or TCR) and do not generalize well across different adaptive immune recognition settings; UniAIR provides a single model that works across these contexts.
method: Unified multimodal representation that integrates sequence and structural information for antibodies, antigens and TCRs into a shared embedding space.
Single, shared architecture trained on diverse immune-recognition datasets to predict mutation effects across contexts and transfer learned patterns between modalities.
Comprehensive evaluation across multiple benchmarks to demonstrate improved cross-context generalization versus specialized models.
impact: For ML practitioners, UniAIR reduces the need for separate models per immune modality and delivers more generalizable mutation-effect predictions—accelerating computational immunology tasks such as therapeutic design and variant risk assessment.
visual_elements: Schematic diagram of the unified model showing inputs (antibody, antigen, TCR sequences/structures) mapped into a shared embedding and mutation-effect output.
Bar chart comparing predictive performance (e.g., accuracy/AUROC) of UniAIR vs modality-specific baselines across antibody, antigen and TCR benchmarks.
Heatmap or residue map visualizing predicted mutation effects on a protein structure (hotspots of impact).
Pipeline flowchart: data sources → multimodal encoding → unified model → mutation-effect predictions → downstream applications (vaccine/antibody design).
paper_title: Generalizable mutation-effect prediction across adaptive immune recognition via unified multimodal framework
paper_authors: Rong Han, Yumeng Zhang, Xiaohong Liu, Lei Fu, Tong Pan
